xray.one_line: AI-native fraud and financial crime prevention for banks, now with Farol, an always-on agent for fraud and AML analysts, and a stated plan to tell good customer agents from bad ones.
xray.what_it_does: Feedzai sells a RiskOps platform that banks, payment networks and acquirers use to detect and stop fraud, scams and money laundering in real time, unifying identity, behavioural, device, transaction and third-party signals from onboarding to remediation, with a separate network score (Feedzai IQ Score) delivered by API. Since 24 September 2026 the platform ships Farol, an embedded agent that retrieves and summarises alert data, analyses rule performance, drafts suspicious activity reports and answers product questions inside RiskOps Studio. Feedzai says it is building two more things for the agentic era: Bring Your Own Agent, to connect banks' own and partner agents to its platform, and detection that checks who authorised a customer's agent, what it may do and whether it still matches its intent. [s1, s4, s14, s3, s2, s6]

situations.title: A customer's agent moves money at a Feedzai bank
reach: The customer's online banking session: the agent logs in on the customer's behalf
The customer's money: the agent pays bills and moves money, and Feedzai expects agents to approve transactions on users' behalf
Real-time payment rails (instant payments such as Pix, and Canada's Real-Time Rail) that clear and settle in seconds, around the clock
Feedzai's real-time scoring of the session and payment: behavioural biometrics, device intelligence, transaction and network signals
Malicious agents that look identical to customers' agents: agent takeovers, agent botnets and agentic malware
asked_our_example: The customer authorises the agent to pay named recurring bills from one account, up to a monthly limit
The agent may not add payees, raise limits or send money to a new beneficiary without the customer confirming
gap: The bank's identity checks were built to verify a human; Feedzai itself says what an agent is allowed to do, on whose authority and within what limits is not yet established, and that live registries of authorised agents will be needed. Until then the customer's limits live only between the customer and the agent.
An instant payment clears in seconds, so any check on whether the agent is still within its limits has to happen before the money moves, not after.
A malicious agent can look identical to the customer's agent; the detection meant to tell them apart is still being built.

situations.title: Farol inside a bank's fraud and AML team
reach: Alert and case data in the institution's fraud and AML stack, and the analyst tools around it
Rule sets, rule performance, coverage gaps and thresholds
Production-ready rule suggestions and what the launch release calls autonomous execution capabilities in risk workflows
Suspicious Activity Report drafts built from case data, about named customers, for local filing requirements
Product documentation, answered in plain language with cited sources
asked_our_example: As Feedzai documents it: agents surface insights and recommendations with transparent reasoning, and analysts verify outcomes and take actions as they see fit
The bank lets Farol read alerts and draft; any rule change goes through challenger testing and a named approver, and only an investigator files a SAR
gap: The launch release speaks of autonomous execution and production-ready rule suggestions, while the product page says analysts take the actions; which actions Farol can take on its own in a given deployment is not public.
A SAR draft about a named customer is one click from case data; Feedzai's own blog says the final call to file must be documented and attributed to a named human.

situations.title: A bank's own agents through Bring Your Own Agent
reach: Feedzai's data, intelligence and workflows, the same context Farol works from
A Model Context Protocol gateway through which connected agents inherit the platform's permissions and audit trail
Third-party partner agents and the bank's choice of model
Bank workflows reached through a secure connection
asked_our_example: The bank's own agent reads alert context for one queue and writes notes, nothing else
A partner agent is read-only and sees no customer data beyond the case it is asked about
gap: Agents that inherit the platform's permissions reach whatever the platform role they run under reaches; how narrowly one connected agent can be scoped is not yet documented.
A partner agent on a model of the bank's choice works from the same context as Feedzai's own agents; where that data goes for inference is outside Feedzai's estate.

questions: When Farol uses what your launch release calls autonomous execution, which actions can it take without an analyst approving them (changing a live rule, closing an alert, filing a SAR), and who in the bank sets that line?

Agents connected through Bring Your Own Agent inherit the platform's permissions: can a bank scope one connected agent below the role it connects under, and is each action attributed to that agent and to a named human in the audit trail?

For Know Your Agent: when a customer's agent arrives at a bank, what will your detection read to learn the limits the customer set, and what happens to a payment that is outside them on a rail that settles in seconds?
Farol runs inside the institution's environment: which model providers does it call, and does any case or customer data leave the bank's estate for inference?
Can a bank export Farol's record of what it retrieved, recommended and who acted on it into its own model risk records, so a supervisor can see who authorised each step?

help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of Feedzai's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
